ORIE 5260 / PART 2 — COURSE PPT ADJUSTED BASELINE

The course PPT approach: adjusted baseline

sᵢ,ₜ = sign(Σₖ₌₀¹¹ rᵢ,ₜ₋ₖ)
σ̂ᵢ,ₜ = Std(rᵢ,₁:ₜ) × √12
wᵢ,ₜ = (1 / Nₜ) × sᵢ,ₜ × 0.40 / σ̂ᵢ,ₜ
  • Expanding volatility requires at least 36 valid monthly observations.
  • Weights formed in month t earn returns in t+1; rebalance monthly.
  • Static uses the same volatility and eligibility, always long.

strategy_backtest_adj.py follows the course PPT approach. The 40% parameter scales individual markets; it is not a portfolio volatility target.

Compounded versus summed momentum signals

Both baselines compound wealth; their historical signal aggregation differs

Example: +20%, then −18%CalculationPosition direction
Rolling compound signal1.20 × 0.82 − 1 = −1.6%Short

  • A controlled signal-only test would hold all other choices fixed.

Why do the static correlations differ?

ComparisonPPT / adjustedRolling
Corr with own static0.0800.385
Signal / volatilitySum / expandingCompound / trailing 12m
Sample1976–20141970.02–2014
  • Possible mechanism: shared recent-volatility scaling may increase co-movement between rolling TSMOM and static.
  • Signal signs, eligibility, and sample periods also differ; their effects are not isolated.
  • Each static benchmark is different. Lower correlation alone does not imply a better strategy.

Observed gap, untested explanation. Align samples and eligibility, then change one component at a time.

ORIE 5260 / PART 4 — SIGNAL EVIDENCE AND RETURN SOURCES

Return attribution: sources and drawdown drivers

  • Commodities: 47.8% of mean return; longs: 81.2%.
  • All classes and both directions contribute positively.
  • Lumber and gold drive gains; soybeans and orange juice detract most.
  • Worst drawdown: AUD, copper, and CAD are major negative contributors.

Monthly contribution cᵢ,ₜ = executed weight × market return. Arithmetic contributions add to portfolio returns; event sums do not decompose compounded MaxDD exactly.

Market regimes: definition and attribution

Adjusted baselineBearBull
Annualized mean10.26%11.13%
Annualized volatility12.60%8.33%

Classification: compound SP futures returns into proxy wealth. If a peak-to-recovery episode reaches a drawdown of at least 20%, label months after the peak through recovery as Bear. If unrecovered, label through sample end. All remaining observed months are Bull.

Decade mean returns: 1970s 10.37%, 1980s 12.22%, 1990s 9.55%, 2000s 12.29%, 2010–2014 7.57%.

Retrospective futures-based labels, not official cash-index regimes or a real-time trading rule.

ORIE 5260 / PART 5 — RISK AND EXTERNAL VALIDATION

Risk concentration under the diagonal model

  • Predicted variance shares: commodities 62.7%, FX 15.9%, FI 11.0%, EQ 10.4%.
  • Effective risk positions: 39.6 instruments, 2.35 classes.
  • Gross exposure sums |weights|; net exposure sums weights.

Diagonal variance = Σ wᵢ²σᵢ², omitting all cross-market covariance terms. Risk share qᵢ = wᵢ²σᵢ² / total; effective positions = 1 / Σqᵢ².

baseline_risk_analysis_output; baseline_performance_output/exposure_summary.csv26 / 30

Validate risk forecasts using fixed weights

HorizonPredicted volRealized volBiasCorrelationExceedance
12 months6.82%9.78%+2.96pp0.1374.8%
3 months6.79%8.87%+2.08pp0.0854.6%

Save formation-month prediction. Freeze those weights and measure annualized volatility over the next H months. Error = realized − predicted; bias = mean error. Exceedance = realized > predicted.

No portfolio volatility target exists here. This tests forecast exceedance, not target breaches. Repeat the same test for each enhanced risk model.
